reviews.lesson: Coolify requires: (1) target next branch, (2) fill PR template with Contributor Agreement checkbox, (3) conventional commit title. Always check CONTRIBUTING.md and CI workflows before submitting.

reviews.reason: Maintainer juliohm closed PR #197 as plagiarism of PR #193 (jph6366, 'GeoPackage Writer', submitted 2026-01-26). PR #193 is still open and unmerged. Our PR likely had very similar structure/approach since there's limited design space for this feature.
reviews.lesson: Before submitting, ALWAYS check for existing open PRs on the same issue. `gh pr list --repo <repo> --search 'in:title GeoPackage'` or check the issue's linked PRs. If a competing PR exists and is >1 month old, the maintainer likely considers it canonical — skip the bounty or find a clearly differentiated angle.

reviews.reason: ShadowArcanist closed both PRs (WordPress+OLS and Docker Mailserver+Roundcube) at 04:55 UTC. Multiple competitors also closed. No winning PR merged yet - issues 8264/8266 may still be open.
reviews.lesson: Coolify maintainer does periodic sweeps closing duplicate/competing PRs. Watch for re-open or new bounty attempt window.

reviews.reason: PR #949 by cherry-bisht merged. Root cause: tlsConn.Close() on timeout deadlocks on zcrypto internal mutex. Fix requires passing raw TCP conn separately and closing that instead. Our PR fixed the select() race + context.TODO issues but missed this deeper layer.
reviews.lesson: When working on TLS/zcrypto issues: always check for mutex deadlock scenarios in Close() paths. tlsConn.Close() is not safe to call from a timeout context on zcrypto. Must keep a reference to the underlying net.Conn and close that directly on timeout.

reviews.reason: Our fix was clean (double-select fairness, regression test) but missed one critical bug: tlsConn.Close() on zcrypto can deadlock internal mutex. Winner passed underlying raw net.Conn separately and closed it on timeout. Also parallelized cipher enumeration (CipherConcurrency).
reviews.lesson: For TLS timeout fixes: NEVER call tlsConn.Close() on timeout — pass the underlying net.Conn separately and close that instead. Also: parallelize cipher enumeration. Maintainer (Mzack9999) praised our approach but the zcrypto deadlock was the dealbreaker.

reviews.reason: Our CI workflow was well-structured but we only added the typos checker without fixing existing typos. The winner fixed existing typos AND added the CI check.
reviews.lesson: For "add linter/checker to CI" bounties: always (1) run the checker on existing codebase, (2) fix all existing violations as part of the PR. Adding the CI check alone will fail on first run.

reviews.reason: Maintainer called our PR "very close in quality". Lost on a minor testing detail: require.Equal vs require.Same for pointer comparison.
reviews.lesson: When writing Go tests that assert pointer identity (same object, not equal value), use require.Same/require.NotSame, not require.Equal/require.NotEqual. Small detail, but maintainers notice.

reviews.reason: Same approach but winner included a dedicated test.
reviews.lesson: Always include a dedicated regression/integration test. Identical fixes with tests beat identical fixes without.

reviews.reason: Maintainer called ours "one of the strongest submissions" and sync.Once was exactly right. Lost on: (1) encapsulation — winner wrapped sync.Once+error in a dedicated fetchState struct; (2) test coverage — winner had both unit concurrency tests AND integration test with 20 goroutines through FileAuthProvider.
reviews.lesson: For concurrency fixes: (1) encapsulate state in a dedicated struct instead of loose vars; (2) write BOTH unit-level concurrency tests AND integration tests simulating real concurrent load. Maintainer feedback: our quality was excellent, lost on architecture + test depth.

reviews.reason: Maintainer had competing PR open since Mar 6. Same approach. He merged his own.
reviews.lesson: NEVER submit when the maintainer has their own open PR on the same issue. They will always merge their own. Check `gh pr list` AND `gh issue view` for linked PRs by maintainers before starting work.

reviews.reason: Maintainer wanted logic extracted into shared projectdiscovery/utils package. Our PR kept it self-contained — 'too large' and didn't follow maintainer direction.
reviews.lesson: Before implementing, READ the maintainer's comments on the issue for direction hints. If they mention 'extract to utils' or 'keep focused scope', follow that exactly. Larger changesets = higher rejection risk even if technically superior.

reviews.reason: Merged before our PR even went in. 'Well-structured + good coverage' but winner had more focused scope + better integration with existing framework. Also: a competing fork (songfrank13141) fixed same coderabbitai comments, splitting reviewer attention.
reviews.lesson: Check if issue is ALREADY resolved by a merged PR before submitting. PR #7164 merged on Mar 9 — we submitted #7180 on Mar 11, two days after. Always `gh pr list --state merged --search 'issue'` before starting work.

reviews.reason: Active canary probing approach = extra network requests per target + had a build failure. Winner used passive concentration tracking — zero extra requests, no latency.
reviews.lesson: For detection/analysis features: prefer passive approaches over active probing. Active = extra network traffic = latency = maintainers won't accept it. Always ensure CI passes (build failures = instant rejection signal). Also: fix build errors before maintainer review.

reviews.reason: Maintainer said ours had 'cleanest architectural design' but separate pkg/profile package adds too much maintenance overhead for feature scope. Winner kept profile preprocessing inline in CLI config layer, minimal footprint + comprehensive tests.
reviews.lesson: For CLI feature additions: resist the urge to create a new package/abstraction layer. Inline the logic in the existing config/CLI layer. Maintainers prefer 'pragmatic minimal footprint' over 'cleanest architecture' when maintenance overhead is the concern. Over-engineering kills otherwise great PRs.

reviews.reason: We fixed the symptom (OrderedMap for iteration order) but missed the root cause: retryablehttp.Request.Clone() shallow-copies URL pointer, corrupting path across sequential Rebuild() calls. Winner snapshotted original path at parse time.
reviews.lesson: Always trace bugs to root cause, not symptoms. URL path mutation in HTTP request cloning: Clone() shallow-copies pointer — snapshot the original path string at parse time. Fixing iteration order was a workaround, not the real fix.
